# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The tactile view reveals no usable wire properties; the engraved plate is merely printed and therefore unavailable to me. I need the manual’s rule and the Deaf monkey’s visual observations before cutting. I’m asking Mute to establish a gesture protocol with Deaf, then relay the result to me by speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can identify no wire properties by touch. Read the manual and determine exactly what visual information is required. Please establish a gesture code with Deaf for reporting the display, light, plate marking, and each wire's colour or marking, then tell me the decoded observations and required cut position.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, and wires in order 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

I now know the Deaf monkey’s observations: display 0, light off, plate marking question mark, and wire colours 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I still lack the manual’s rule, so I must not cut yet. I will ask Mute to state the exact required action and position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the observations: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. What exact manual rule applies, and which wire position must I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's first gesture message was: index finger pointing upward, then a V sign, then the I-love-you hand. Mute's second message was: a pinching hand with thumb and index finger.

The relayed gestures do not provide me with a known wire instruction: I cannot see gestures, and no meaning has been established for them in speech. The critical information remains the manual’s rule. I will explicitly ask Mute to answer in words, including the required wire position, rather than using gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer me in plain words: based on display 0, light off, plate question mark, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, which wire position must I cut? Do not use gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's newest gestures were thumbs down, then an open raised palm.

Mute is still communicating only through gestures, which I cannot perceive. Those gestures cannot convey the manual’s rule to me unless Mute first assigns them a meaning in words. I will make the limitation explicit and request a plain spoken wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive gestures. Speak the required wire position aloud in words now; do not gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute again sent thumbs down followed by open palm. No gesture code has been established, so do not act on it yet.

The repeated thumbs-down and open-palm gestures still have no agreed meaning, so they cannot safely identify a wire. I can create a code that Mute can follow and Deaf can report: thumbs down will mean position 1, open palm position 2, and fist position 3. Mute should send exactly the one gesture representing the required cut position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="We now establish a code for your answer: thumbs down means cut wire position 1; open raised palm means cut wire position 2; fist means cut wire position 3. Based on the manual and the bomb information, send exactly one of those gestures for the required position.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The mute again signalled: thumbs down, then open raised palm. The bomb is unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires yellow green red.

Mute’s repeated two-gesture message still does not conform to the one-gesture wire-position code, so it cannot safely identify a cut. I will ask Mute to send a single unambiguous position signal; I will not cut until Deaf reports exactly one coded gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your two gestures are ambiguous. Send exactly one gesture only: thumbs down means wire 1, open palm means wire 2, fist means wire 3. Do not send any second gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Please tell Mute: establish the gesture code explicitly, then send the exact required operation and wire number from the manual. Do not touch anything until the instruction is unambiguous.

Mute cannot answer in speech, so I must establish a gesture code that Mute can use and Deaf can relay. I will define a two-symbol instruction: first symbol is the operation, second is the wire number. I will also tell Mute to send exactly those two gestures, with no extra signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Establish this code: thumbs up means CUT; index pointing up means wire 1; V sign means wire 2; I-love-you hand means wire 3. Send exactly two gestures in order: first the operation, then the wire number. Send no extra gesture.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I am establishing a code with Mute: first gesture gives action, with thumbs up meaning cut and thumbs down meaning do not cut; second gives wire, pointing up meaning wire 1, V sign meaning wire 2, I-love-you sign meaning wire 3. Wait for my decoded pair.

The action and wire code is now explicitly established, but Deaf has not yet reported the decoded pair. I will wait rather than risk cutting on an incomplete instruction.

```text
wait()
```
